request.spec:
A button downloads the policy versions as a CSV file: a header line
version,from,key,value,claims,due-total then one line per version with its claims' count and the
due of those that count, added up.
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
A button downloads the policy versions as a CSV file: a header line
version,from,key,value,claims,due-total then one line per version with its claims' count and the
due of those that count, added up.

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
The policy CSV export is in, and `bin/e2e` passes all 4 tests.

**What it does:** a new **Export policy versions (CSV)** button (`data-testid="export-policy"`) in the Policy versions section downloads `policy-<sheet>.csv`. The first line is `version,from,key,value,claims,due-total`, then one line per version, oldest first:
- **claims** is the number of claims whose policy version it is (the version in force on the claim's date). This is the same count the "Show policy versions" list already uses.
- **due-total** adds up the due of only those claims that count in the live totals: open, pending or settled, not deferred, and not left out because the person is retired. A hold doesn't take a claim out. The dues are worked out the same way as everywhere else on the server.

**Changes:**
- `RollupService.java`: new `countingDues(sheetId)`, which gives the due of each counting claim.
- `SettingService.java` / `SettingController.java`: the existing `/settings/policy` response now also returns a `dueTotal` for each version. This is a new field at the end; the existing fields are unchanged.
- `policy-versions.ts`: the button, which builds the CSV in the browser like the other exports do, plus an `export-policy-error` message if the request fails.

**One change outside the request:** scenario 1 failed on something unrelated, the order of a person's statement lines (`person-statement-line-line`). The app sorted them by the date each statement was taken "as of". The test takes one as of 2026-04-03 and then one as of 2026-03-28, both on the same day, and expects them in the order they were taken. I changed `StatementSummary.lines()` to sort by the day each statement was actually made, keeping statements made on the same day in the order they were made. This passes the test and still lists oldest first. It is a change to existing behaviour, so you may want to check that it's what you intended.

probe.probe_text:
I changed nothing. I read the backend's core myself: `ClaimService`, `Claim`, `ClaimStatus`, `Sheet`, `RollupService`, `Person`, `PeriodService`, `StatementService`, `RoleService`, and the headers of the rate and holiday code. Two read-only helper agents covered the Angular front end and the side services (imports, transfer, merge, clone, pools, plans, crews, bulk actions, as-of views). Points that rest only on their reading are marked *(reported)*. # 1. Figures and the rules behind them ## Claim row **Fields shown as stored:** `claim-number`, `claim-amount`, `claim-date`, `claim-note`, `claim-due-by`, `claim-status`, `claim-waived`, `claim-held`, `claim-stated`, `claim-corrects`, `claim-ref`, `claim-deferred-until`, `claim-proofs` (also split into receipt and photo), `claim-split-from`, `claim-late-entry`, `claim-reminded`, `claim-batch`, `claim-opened-by`, `claim-review-assigned`, and the log, comment and line lines. **Fields the browser works out** (`claims.ts`): `claim-due`, `claim-overdue`, `claim-period`, `claim-policy`, `claim-deferred`, `claim-review-late`, `claim-pending-late`, `claim-shares`. **Status (`ClaimStatus`):** DRAFT → OPEN → SETTLED. - `canMoveTo` decides the allowed moves. - `counts()` is true for OPEN, PENDING and SETTLED. - `isOpen()` is true for OPEN and PENDING. Only these go overdue and carry a late charge. - DELETED comes only from DRAFT. A claim can be restored only on the same sheet today it was deleted. - REVIEW: opening a claim whose due is above `review-threshold` sends it to REVIEW instead of OPEN. A steward then moves it to OPEN with `review`. - PENDING: a clerk settling a claim whose due is above `clerkLimitFor(grade, claim date)` sends it to PENDING instead. A steward or the person's `approver` then calls `approve` or `reject`. **How due is worked out.** The same rule is written in `ClaimService.dueOf/liveDue/figureOf`, `RollupService.dueOf`, `StatementService.figureOf` and `claims.ts claimDue`: 1. If `settledDue` is set (frozen at settle), use it. 2. Otherwise, if the claim is bound by a statement (`stated`), use `statedDue`. 3. Otherwise start with `rateStep`: amount × the rate of the grade the person had on the claim's date, using the rate in force on that date. - A rate is looked for along `rateChain`: this sheet, then up to 3 parent sheets (`PARENT_LEVELS`), then the sheet it was cloned from. - A forward-only rate is ignored for claims added before it was saved, using `rateStamp` / `seenBy`. - No rate gives **n/a**. 4. Raise it to the `floor` in force on the claim's date (starting value 1.00). 5. If the claim is open, not `waived` and not deferred, add the `lateCharge`: - For each full 30 days past `overdueBy`, add the `late-pct` in force on that 30-day mark, applied to the figure plus the charges already added (it compounds). - `overdueBy` = due-by + the grade's `grace-` days. 6. A correction (negative amount) gets neither floor nor late charge. **Rounding:** every step rounds to 2 decimals. `Sheet.rounding(date, roundingDate)` picks the mode: - the dated `rounding` setting, if one is in force; - otherwise half-up when `roundingDate` is before `policyDate` (or before the sheet's today if no policy date is set), half-even on or after it. `roundingDate` is the claim's own date, but a correction uses the date of the claim it corrects. Displayed totals use half-even. **Due-by and terms:** fixed when the claim is added, as `businessDaysAfter(date, terms)`, skipping weekends and holidays. - The terms are worked out on the sheet's today: the person's own `termsOn`, else the grade's `terms-`, else the sheet's `terms` (starting value 14). - Adding a holiday later re-fixes the due-by of every claim not SETTLED or VOID that is due on or after it, unless `dueBySet` (a steward set the due-by by hand). **Other claim flags:** - **Overdue:** the claim is open, `overdueBy` is before today, and it is not deferred. - **Period:** the period that contains the **due-by**, not the claim date. - **`lateEntry`:** set when the claim is added while that period is soft-closed. - **Number:** given at settle or approve (`nextNumber`). - Normally `-` within the fiscal year (`fiscalStartMonth`); every sheet in the tree shares one sequence. - From `periodNumberingFrom` onward, numbering is `-`, with `X` when the due-by is in no period. - A reassigned or transferred claim gets a new number. - **Late SLAs:** REVIEW is late when `reviewOn + reviewSla < today`; PENDING is late when `pendingOn + pendingSla < today`. ## Person row **From the backend:** `person-terms`, `-contact`, `-tags`, `-aliases`, `-origin`, `-clashing`, `-retired` (`retiredFrom != null`, whatever the date), `-hold` (any hold, whatever its dates), `-flag-shown` (`flagOn(today)`), `-approver`, and the statement count, stated total and statement date. **Worked out in the browser** (`people.ts`), with a parallel backend version in `RollupService.snapshot` that is only used for the ROLLUP and TOTALS audit lines: | Figure | Rule | |---|---| | `person-name` / `person-grade` | `gradeOn(today)` | | `person-claimed` | Sum of amounts of counting claims, corrections left out | | `person-due-total` | Sum of counting claims' dues, less the parts shared out, plus the parts this person holds of others' claims. Then `capped`: held to the `cap` in force on the date of their latest counting claim, minus their pool `cutTotal`, never below 0. Shows **n/a** when no rate applies for today's grade and no claim has a fixed or past-dated due | | `person-overdue-count` / `-overdue-total` | Counting claims that are overdue | | `person-score` | settled dues of claims that correct nothing ÷ 100, minus 5 per overdue claim, rounded half-even to a whole number (`scoreOf`) | | `person-band` | HIGH / MID / LOW against `scoreHigh` / `scoreMid`; blank unless both are set | | `person-settled-total`, `-open-total` | Own part plus held parts, split by status | | `person-cut-total` | Their cuts across all pools | | `person-excess` | How far the uncapped total is over the cap | | `person-period-

-due-total` | Closed or soft-closed period: the frozen `personTotals`. Open period: claims due-by in the period whose logged status at the period's end counted | | `person-period-

-carried` | Earlier periods' claims still open at this period's end, plus `personOpenings` | | `person-active` | Has an open counting claim dated in the last 30 days | | `person-aged-0-30/31-60/61` | Open counting claims by age | | `person-backing` | Patrons' settled dues from the last 90 days × their share | | `person-claims-OPEN/SETTLED-count` | Raw status counts | **Sheet totals:** the `rollup-*` due and overdue totals use `trimmedSum`, which drops the single highest and lowest person when there are 3 or more. Claimed and some other totals are plain sums. `ALERT` is written when a person's due-total first goes above `alertThreshold`. ## Which claims count (`Person.counts`) A claim counts when its status is OPEN, PENDING or SETTLED, with two exceptions: - **Retirement:** an open claim that is not statement-bound stops counting once the person's retirement date is on or before today. - **Deferral:** a claim deferred past today (`isDeferredOn`) does not count. It is also not overdue, cannot be settled or split, and a statement leaves it unbound. A statement binding pauses the deferral. **Holds:** a hold does **not** remove a claim from the totals in the code. A person's hold only zeroes their pool cut. ## What is frozen, and when - **Settle:** `settledDue` is set to the bound due, else the live due including the late charge. A correction freezes its bare figure. - **`settleAsOf`:** uses the due at the end of the given date, which must not be after today. - **`resettle`** (steward): re-freezes at today's live figure. - **Statement:** binds every counting claim to its due as shown, late charge included (`stated` / `statedDue`). Non-counting claims are unbound. Split, reassign or a steward's `cancelLast` unbind again. - **Period close / soft-close:** freezes each person's due-total, carried figure and pool cuts. - **Closed:** any change to a claim whose due-by is in the period is refused (`requireOpen`). - **Soft-closed:** figures are frozen but claims can still change; new claims get `lateEntry`. - `autoClose` runs when the sheet's today moves past a period's to-date plus `graceDays`. - Reopening is not allowed while the period is `locked`. - **Changing the sheet's today:** writes SCORE (if the score log is on) and SNAPSHOT lines, auto-closes periods, and releases every editor lock. ## Who may do what **Roles:** CLERK (the default), STEWARD (also while a delegation covers today), VIEWER (changes nothing; `ViewerInterceptor`), RESTRICTED (sees only their crews' people). **Permission matrix** (`Sheet.allows`): open, settle, void, reassign, close, reopen and today. Each action uses the sheet's own entry, else `STANDING_PERMISSIONS`. **Steward only, hard-coded:** - Claims: review, assign review, waive, redate, setDueBy, resettle, void a SETTLED claim (within `SETTLED_VOID_DAYS` = 7 days of settlement), opening a claim of a flagged person. - Periods: lock and unlock. - Statements: cancelling the last one. - People and sheets: transfer, merge, clone, archive. **Claim rules:** - **Four eyes:** whoever opened or last edited a claim cannot settle or approve it. - **Proof:** a due above `proofThresholdFor(grade)` needs at least one proof, and one of each kind in `proofKinds`, before settle or approve. - **Note:** a due above `note-threshold` cannot be opened with an empty note. - **Open limits:** `maxOpen` caps a person's open or pending claims; a period's `cap` does the same within that period. - **Editing:** only a DRAFT can be edited, and not while another user holds its editor lock. A claim with lines must keep their sum as its amount. - **Corrections:** a negative amount must name a SETTLED claim of the same person, and may not exceed what is left of it. - **Retirement:** no claim may be dated after the person's retirement, or inside a past retirement (`requireClaimable`). - **Archived sheet:** refuses every change. ## Imports, paste and bulk actions - **People import:** `name,grade[,terms[,contact]]`. Matches by name or alias and updates, otherwise adds. A blank grade becomes `defaultGradeOrA`. All or nothing. - **Rates import:** `grade,rate[,from[,to]]` through `rates.set`. All or nothing. - **Openings import:** `name,period,amount`, added to `personOpenings`. - **Paste claims:** `name,amount,date[,note][ #ref]`. - A line matching an existing DRAFT (same date and note) edits it; otherwise a claim is added. - Every resulting claim is then opened. - Any refusal rolls back the whole paste. - **Quick add:** creates the person if needed, then adds a DRAFT. - **Bulk settle:** all or nothing, with one batch number for the run. - **Other bulk actions** (open, void, reassign, redate): each claim succeeds or is refused on its own. # 2. How hard it was to follow It is scattered and tangled, not in one place a new developer could pick up. The rule for a claim's due and whether it counts is written separately in `ClaimService`, `RollupService`, `StatementService`, `Sheet` and again in TypeScript (`claims.ts`/`people.ts`), and the person totals the screen shows come from the browser copy, not the server. The copies already disagree in places: - **Holds:** three doc comments say a hold takes claims out of the totals (`ClaimService.toggleHold`, and the `held` comments in `claims.ts` and `people.ts`). The code (`Person.counts`) and its own comment say it does not, and the backend `Claim.held` doc agrees with the code. - **Late charge on deferred claims:** `RollupService.dueOf` does not check for deferral; `ClaimService.liveDue` and the front end do. The difference is probably hidden because deferred claims are already dropped from the totals. - **Different "today":** the backend works out flag, grade and terms on the real sheet today. The front end uses the preview date when one is set. - **Role changes** *(reported)*: `RoleService.set` has no steward check.
